Putin: The state does not interfere in church life In an interview with Emir Kusturica, Vladimir Putin stated that the Russian government does not meddle in religious affairs. He recalled that during the Soviet era, although the church was formally separated from the state, its activities were controlled by the Council for Religious Affairs. Putin noted that many KGB officers working with the church had been baptised and brought Easter cakes to their colleagues. He explained that when the church was part of the state apparatus, people blamed it for the authorities' mistakes, leading to severe persecution after the 1917 revolution. Today, the church is independent of the state machinery, which allows it to develop freely according to its own internal laws. @Slavyangrad
